acceptance_criteria.criterion: NO CODE SHIPS FROM THIS ROW -- it is an OWNER GATE, not a build. Its entire deliverable is a pick among named outcomes; each outcome's executable steps already live on a CHILD row, and the work happens THERE. "Ruling = pick the child(ren) to unblock."

THE DECISION PACKET IS READ BEFORE RULING. Paper arpss-anon-exposure-ruling-2026-08-17 carries the live per-host census, the flip mechanism, the dependent-tool roster and each outcome's executable steps. The row says "READ IT to rule" -- a ruling made without it is ungrounded, however reasonable it sounds.

THE RULING NAMES EXACTLY ONE OF THE THREE OUTCOMES, and thereby which child to unblock: (A) STAY PUBLIC -- no change, the current shipped state, no child needed; (B) STAY PUBLIC + ANON PROJECTION -- title-only anon reads via an Envelope.render/3 projection gate, child arpss-anon-projection-gate; (C) FLIP PRIVATE per host -- code default + per-host data migration + per-host console read of pull_provenance FIRST, child arpss-flip-private-migration. The rider may accompany C: SHRINK THE HOST SET, depublishing or deleting the frozen primary and muscle-1 corpora (child arpss-shrink-host-set), discharging them WITHOUT touching visibility.

THE CUSTOMER HOST IS WEIGHED EXPLICITLY AND THE CENSUS IS RE-MEASURED FIRST. The live anon census recorded 2026-08-17 was guerrilla 6212t/776p, muscle-1 3139t/551p (frozen), primary 0t/15p, and gyldendal 13t/51p -- and gyldendal is a REAL CUSTOMER. That census is days old; re-measure before ruling, and say what the chosen outcome means for the customer host specifically rather than for the fleet in aggregate.

IF (C): THE MECHANISM CONSTRAINT IS HONOURED IN THE RULING ITSELF. schema.visibility=public is a CODE declaration re-asserted EVERY BOOT for production Default-slot rows (pull_provenance-stamped hosts skip; non-production datasets are never re-asserted), so a flip is CODE PLUS MIGRATION and "neither sufficient alone." A ruling for C that authorises only one half authorises something that will silently revert at the next boot.

IF (C): THE HARD DEPENDENCY IS SEQUENCED, NOT JUST MENTIONED. arpss-pr-task-gate-token-plumbing MUST merge and be green BEFORE any guerrilla flip, because the pr-task-gate reads guerrilla TOKENLESSLY and hard-reds main -- INCLUDING the fix itself -- on a task 404. Ruling C without sequencing that first authorises an action that breaks main and blocks its own remedy.

THE OWNER CLOSES THIS -- AND SILENCE IS ALREADY A RULING, WHICH IS WHY IT MUST NOT SIT. The row states "silence on this gate = accept option A (stay public)." So an indefinitely-open row here misrepresents the board: a decision has in fact been made by default. Either an explicit ruling is recorded, or option A is recorded AS the ruling with a date and the reason it was accepted by default.

documents.close_reason:
OWNER RULING RECORDED, 2026-08-22. The owner ruled directly; this is no longer silence-accepts-the-default.

RULING, SPLIT PER HOST as the packet's own recommendation urges ('this is not one exposure, it is three; ruling them as one question is what kept this open'):

(1) gyldendal (CUSTOMER, 13t/51p anon @2026-08-17T08:37Z) -> FLIP TASK+PAPER PRIVATE, scoped to that host. This is the packet's marked default and the owner ruled it explicitly rather than by silence. Unblocks the gyldendal arm of arpss-flip-private-migration. NOT EXECUTED BY THIS ROW: the packet requires an explicit YES on the child before the migration runs its gyldendal arm, because customer-host actions never ride silence. The pr-task-gate token dependency does NOT bind here - it binds only a guerrilla flip.

(2) guerrilla (6212t/776p, the live working ledger) -> STAY PUBLIC (outcome A). Owner-ruled explicitly. Grounds, per the packet: the binding pr-task-gate, seal.mjs and reland-check all read it TOKENLESSLY, the corpus is dev-internal, and the only address leak is @sanity.io seed data. Revisit toward B (arpss-anon-projection-gate) or C if customer-adjacent content ever lands here.

(3) primary + muscle-1 (0t/15p stale; 3139t/551p frozen since 2026-07-26) -> NOT RULED IN THIS PASS. The packet marks these per-wave and non-blocking, and its default is SHRINK via arpss-shrink-host-set (depublish the dead corpora, discharging the exposure with no visibility flip). Left open deliberately rather than swept in on a ruling the owner was not asked for. Its destructive step separately requires an explicit YES after a dead-host probe confirms no active writer.

(4) Token plumbing (arpss-pr-task-gate-token-plumbing + provisioning BARKPARK_TASK_TOKEN) -> UNCHANGED and still owed. Per-wave under ruling (2); it is a HUMAN provisioning step and remains the sole unblocker for any future guerrilla flip.

HONEST GAP IN THIS CLOSE: criterion 3 requires the live census be RE-MEASURED before ruling. It was NOT re-measured. The cloud session is expired (bp cloud and GET /v1/sites both 401) and only the user's bp login renews it; I did not substitute a credential to manufacture a number. The ruling therefore rests on the 2026-08-17T08:37Z figures carried in the packet, which the packet itself warns drift (guerrilla papers moved 775->776 mid-wave). The customer-host call is robust to that drift - 13t/51p is nonzero and the argument is categorical, not quantitative - but anyone executing the gyldendal arm should re-measure first. Also unverified: the packet notes bp cloud status was auth-blocked during ITS verification too, so a FIFTH host could exist and has never been probed.

Criterion 1 (read the packet before ruling): the packet WAS read before the final ruling, but not before my first framing - I initially put all three hosts to the owner as a single three-way choice, which is precisely the error the packet names as the reason this row stayed open. I corrected the framing and re-asked per host. Recording that sequence rather than presenting the ruling as clean.
documents.description:
OWNER GATE (not a build). Rule how task+paper schema.visibility should behave. The full decision packet -- live per-host census, flip mechanism, dependent-tool roster, and each outcome's executable steps -- is the decision Paper arpss-anon-exposure-ruling-2026-08-17 (READ IT to rule). Verified this wave: schema.visibility=public is a CODE declaration re-asserted every boot for production Default-slot rows (pull_provenance-stamped hosts skip; non-production datasets never re-asserted), so a flip is code+migration, neither sufficient alone. Live anon 2026-08-17: guerrilla 6212t/776p, muscle-1 3139t/551p (frozen), primary 0t/15p, gyldendal (CUSTOMER) 13t/51p. THREE OUTCOMES, pick one child to unblock:
(A) STAY PUBLIC -- no change; the current shipped state. Recommended default ONLY if the exposure is judged acceptable. No child needed.
(B) STAY PUBLIC + ANON PROJECTION -- title-only anon reads via an Envelope.render/3 projection gate. Child: arpss-anon-projection-gate.
(C) FLIP PRIVATE per host -- code default + per-host data migration + per-host console read of pull_provenance FIRST. Child: arpss-flip-private-migration. HARD DEPENDENCY: arpss-pr-task-gate-token-plumbing MUST merge + be green BEFORE any guerrilla flip (the pr-task-gate reads guerrilla tokenlessly and hard-reds main -- INCLUDING the fix -- on a task 404).
Plus a cheapest-for-dead-hosts option that rides alongside C for the two frozen corpora: SHRINK THE HOST SET -- depublish/delete the frozen primary + muscle-1 (child arpss-shrink-host-set), discharging them without touching visibility. Ruling = pick the child(ren) to unblock; silence on this gate = accept option A (stay public).
documents.disposition_reason: OWNER GATE DISCHARGED 2026-08-22 by explicit owner ruling, not by silence. Split per host: gyldendal (CUSTOMER) FLIP PRIVATE; guerrilla STAY PUBLIC; primary+muscle-1 left unruled (per-wave, packet default is SHRINK); token plumbing still owed as a human provisioning step. NOTHING WAS EXECUTED: the gyldendal arm of arpss-flip-private-migration still requires a separate explicit YES on that child before it runs, per the packet's rule that customer-host actions never ride silence. Census NOT re-measured (bp login expired); ruling rests on 2026-08-17T08:37Z figures and anyone executing should re-measure. Full reasoning in close_reason.
